tasks.description: The export button should be added to the sales report page. It should be visible and clickable when the report is displayed. The button should have a clear label indicating its purpose.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sales report page is loaded, when the user clicks the export button, then a download of the report is initiated.

tasks.description: Create a backend endpoint that generates the CSV for the requested report and streams the response to the client. This should be done in a way that keeps memory usage bounded regardless of report size.
acceptance_criteria: Given a large sales report, when the export endpoint is called, then the response is streamed to the client without running out of memory.

tasks.description: Allow the user to choose which columns to include in the export before downloading. The generated CSV should only include the selected columns, in the displayed order.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sales report page is loaded, when the user selects specific columns, then only those columns are included in the exported CSV.

tasks.description: Encode the CSV per RFC 4180. This includes quoting fields containing commas, double quotes, or newlines, and escaping embedded double quotes by doubling them.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sales report with special characters, when the report is exported to CSV, then the CSV is properly encoded according to RFC 4180.

tasks.description: The first row of the CSV should contain the human-readable column names for the selected columns.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sales report is exported to CSV, when the CSV is opened, then the first row contains the human-readable column names.

tasks.description: Integrate the export button, streaming export endpoint, column selection, RFC 4180 escaping, and header row into a cohesive export feature.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sales report page is loaded, when the user clicks the export button, then a properly formatted CSV is downloaded.
